The turbine configuration consists of 21 vane airfoils and 52 rotor blades, with a 2-vane/5-rotor blade count approximation used in the simulations.
The rotor tip clearance was set at a typical value of approximately 2.5% of the rotor height.
The inlet Mach number is 0.12, the inlet static pressure is 15.2 MPa, and the inlet static temperature is 1232 K.
The rotor rotates at 31,300 RPM, and the Reynolds number (based on the inlet conditions and the rotor axial chord) is approximately 5 x 10^5.
The ratio of the rotor exit static pressure to vane inlet total pressure is 0.1875.
The operating fluid in the turbine is a gaseous hydrogen mixture.

The meanline analysis predicts insignificant changes in the total-to-total and total-to-static efficiencies for the variable specific heats case, while the Navier-Stokes analysis predicts a small decrease in the efficiencies.
Both the meanline and Navier-Stokes analyses predict a slight decrease in the work extracted by the turbine for the variable specific heats case.
The Navier-Stokes results indicate increased pressure unsteadiness in the endwall regions for the variable specific heats case.
The average value of y+, the non-dimensional distance of the first grid line above the surface, was approximately 1.5 for the airfoil surfaces and 3.5 for the endwalls.
The total number of grid points used to discretize the turbine was 1,363,022.
The simulations were run on seven 250 MHz processors of an SGI Origin2000, with each iteration requiring approximately 16 seconds of computation time.
The time periodicity of the solutions was determined by plotting pressure traces at different points along the airfoil surfaces.
The coefficients for the variable specific heats equation for hydrogen are provided for temperatures between 300 and 1000 K, and 1000 and 5000 K.
The addition of the variable specific heats subroutine resulted in less than a 5% increase in CPU time.
